newsitem.title: USA: Jacor buys option for 2 Ohio radio outlets.
newsitem.headline: Jacor buys option for 2 Ohio radio outlets.

text.p: Jacor Communications Inc on Monday said it bought a $2.5 million option to purchase two radio stations in Youngstown, Ohio.
The final purchase price for the stations, located in Ohio's eighth-largest broadcast area, is $11 million, the company said in a statement.
The stations, WKGN-AM and WKBN-FM, belong to WKBN Broadcasting Corp. Any purchase is subject to regulatory review, the company said.
Jacor said it was the third-largest U.S. radio group in terms of revenues. In 1996, total revenues topped $223.8 million, the company told Reuters.

Jacor said owned, operated or represented about 154 radio stations in 34 U.S. broadcast areas. It also owns Radio-Active Media, the syndicator of radio programs featuring political commentator Rush Limbaugh.
The company's stock rose 1-1/8 to close at 43-5/8 Monday.
